text:
maria: Heads up — CI perf spike on canary after yesterday's runtime merge (PR #4821). continuous-batcher token/sec dropped ~28% on seqlen=512 profile runs.
perf-ci-bot: perf-regression detected: token_sec -28% vs baseline on e2e/profile-run-512 (link: https://ci/redwood/perf/236123) :warning:
noah: ugh. is this the kernel-selection change we merged? saw 'prefer_layout_swap=true' in the diff.
eli: I started a quick bisect on the canary image. preliminary points to a kernel switch + slightly larger batch windows.
maria: canary was held, we stopped the rollout at ~10% traffic. deploy-bot: rollout paused by policy (canary_hold).
noah: what do perf traces show? kv hitrate? queueing?
eli: attaching a tiny profiler excerpt (from post-merge canary):
```
# continuous-batcher trace summary
step,avg_batch,avg_latency_ms,tokens_sec,kv_hitrate
1,18,24.2,6200,0.72
2,22,28.9,4500,0.54  # token/sec drop correlating with kv hitrate dip
3,20,26.1,4800,0.58
```
maria: baseline (pre-merge) numbers for same workload were ~8500 tokens/sec, avg_batch 14. so token/sec down and batch size up.
noah: that smells like our scheduler heuristics nudged batch_window up for late-arriving requests, coupling with the new kernel that prefers coalesced copies — more waiting, worse kv locality.
eli: bisect landed on commit abc123 (kernel: fallback heuristics + layout swap rule). when we force the old kernel selector at runtime, tokens/sec returns to ~8000 in microbench.
maria: good signal. is kv cache eviction different? maybe cache growth + eviction thrash with larger batches. any logs?
eli: kv eviction counters show spikes aligned with batch drain times. extracting trace now.
onoah: can we run microbench matrix: pre-merge vs post-merge with kv warm/cold, seq lens [64,256,512], and kernel toggles? I can script that.
maria: please do. we need a short-term mitigation: either pin kernel selector to old behavior on canary/dedicated or reduce batch_window to prior value.
noah: I'll prepare a targeted revert PR (just the kernel selector change) and a runtime flag to force old behavior. if QA/benchmarks look good we can apply a canary patch.
eli: also recommend adding a kv-hitrate alert to perf CI so small regressions don't slip by. current alert threshold too loose.
maria: agree. logging action items: 1) noah: revert PR + runtime flag (ETA 2h). 2) eli: run microbench matrix and kv traces (ETA 3h). 3) noah+maria: coordinate canary patch rollout and signal if token/sec recovers. 4) infra: lower perf CI alert threshold for kv-hitrate.
perf-ci-bot: note: perf-alert created #perf-789, assigned to eng-runtime.
deploy-bot: canary hold remains active until manual resume.
noah: starting revert PR now: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/4830. linking perf artifacts in PR.
eli: if revert fixes, we'll follow with a thorough test to understand why kernel change increased avg_batch — probably scheduling heuristic interaction.
maria: thanks — let's keep thread updates brief. ping when microbench finishes or revert is merged. :thumbsup:
